penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Legacy server patching, EOL OS migration, and Plesk remediation are hands-on technical tasks requiring per-customer manual work by a skilled sysadmin — cannot be automated by Claude + this tooling.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Scoping a migration or retainer engagement for a client's live production server requires discovery calls and client sign-off at each step.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Managing live infrastructure for paying clients involves incident response and human judgement under time pressure — not async-automatable.

rationale: The pain is real and the buyer (freelance sysadmin or agency owner managing client servers) is identifiable and willing to pay, but this is fundamentally a done-for-you technical services play requiring a skilled human sysadmin to actually do the work. Claude cannot SSH into a Plesk server, patch PHP on an EOL Ubuntu instance, or coordinate a live migration — this is not buildable as an autonomous micro-service with this factory's tooling. The operational_autonomy score of 2 reflects that every customer engagement requires deep per-customer manual work.
solution_plan: Not recommended to build with this factory. The underlying service is managed server work — it requires a human sysadmin with root access, not an AI content or data pipeline. A non-technical solo operator cannot fulfill this without subcontracting technical labor, which changes the unit economics entirely. If Youval has sysadmin expertise, this is a viable freelance service, but it is out of scope for an autonomous Claude factory. Possible adjacent angle worth validating separately: a Claude-generated 'legacy server migration checklist + risk report' sold as a $49 PDF to agencies — low touch, fully automatable, tests willingness to pay before committing to anything operational.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy gate (score 2, minimum 7). Fails buildability_with_ai gate (score 4, minimum 6). Total 2.2 far below min_total_to_validate. Drop.
